column2: ENGLISH
The company rides east. The road runs past the Wastes, through the mountains and along the Ogre road. Two defeats, or the death of its leader, will end the quest.
The company rides on.
The company is bloodied. One more defeat like this and the quest is over.
Every lord of Kislev's gods gains §YUrsun Wakes§! for 25 years.
Every lord of Kislev's gods suffers §YThe Long Sleep§! for 25 years: bears turn on men and the cults of the Dark Gods grow bold.
The hearths stay cold until you bring Dazh's flame home. The §YRelight the Hearth§! decision sends for it.
Keep the oath to the end of the war and win, and Tor rewards you. Lose the war, and you are an oath-breaker.
The Khan-Queen speaks to you.

A bear walked into the great hall at dusk, through the open doors and past the guards, and lay down before the hearth as if it were dying. It was gone by morning. Since then the dreams have come every night: a bear the size of a hill, lying in the dark under the mountains with a black wound in its side. Last night the stars burned red over the High Pass. The priests do not need to say it. The Father of Bears is wounded, somewhere in the east.
Ursun calls. We ride east.
Omens are for old women.

The company is gathering in the courtyard: riders of the Circle with bear pelts over their mail, a priest with the old maps, packhorses loaded for a year on the road. The road east runs along the edge of the Wastes, over the World's Edge and down the Ogre road toward the High Pass. Someone must lead them.
Send the best rider of the Circle.
I will lead them myself.

At the edge of the Wastes the snow turns grey and the wind smells of iron. On the third day the scouts come back at a gallop: a Chaos warband is on the company's trail, a hundred riders under a banner of flayed skin, and they are closing.
Turn and fight.
Hide in the snow and let them pass.

The pass through the World's Edge is full of greenskins. Their fires burn on every ledge, and the drums go on all night. There is another way, a goat track over the glacier, but it adds months to the road and the ice has killed better riders than these.
Fight through the pass.
Take the long way over the ice.

On the Ogre road the company is stopped by a wall of meat and iron: an Ogre tribe of the Mountains of Mourning, camped across the road. Their Tyrant is happy to let the little men pass, for a price in gold. Or he is happy to eat them. He does not much mind which.
Pay the toll.
Cut our way through.

They found it in a cave under the mountains, where the riders' torches could not reach the roof. A bear the size of a hill, breathing slow and deep, with a black wound in its side that smells of the Wastes. The priest is weeping. The riders have taken off their helms. Ursun lies here, and he is waiting for something.
Offer him our blood.
Offer him a life.
Take a tooth, for a relic.

Word has come out of the east, and it is good. The Father of Bears was wounded, and now he is healed. In the forests of Kislev the bears are calm again, and men feel stronger than they did. The priests of Ursun are telling everyone who will listen that he is awake.
Ursun is awake!

There is no word from the east, and there will be none. The company is gone, or the god turned his face from them. The priests of Ursun go about with ashes on their foreheads, and in the forests the bears have grown strange and angry. The Father of Bears sleeps, and while he sleeps the cults of the Dark Gods grow bold.
Ursun sleeps.

A bear came out of the forest at noon, walked into the village beyond the walls and went for the first person it saw. [ursun_mauled.GetTitledName] was there. The priests say the bears have forgotten men since the god fell asleep.
Hunt it down.
Let the priests try to calm it.

The Waking Day feast is at its loudest when [ursun_mocker.GetTitledName] climbs onto the table, a horn of mead in each hand, and asks the hall why anyone should drink to a god who sleeps half the year like a lazy dog. Someone laughs. Nobody else does. The priest of Ursun is looking at you.
Drag him outside and teach him respect.
He is drunk. Let it go.
Let him say it to a bear.

One young man has won every contest at Waking Day: the stone, the log, the wrestling and the drinking horn. He kneels before you with his chest still heaving and asks for a place in your service. He has nothing but his strength and a borrowed shirt.
Make him a champion of my court.
Send him to the Circle of the Bear.
Give him a purse and send him on his way.

The enemy is in the capital, and the flame in the temple of Dazh has gone out. It has burned since the founding, and every hearth in the realm was lit from it. The old women say that while the hearth is cold, no child born will be blessed and no house will be warm. The priests agree with them.
Send a priest of the Rota of the Dawn to carry the flame back.
Send to the great temple in Kislev for the flame.
The flame can wait.

The flame has come home in an iron lantern, carried at a walk through the snow and never once allowed to gutter. The priests light the temple hearth from it, and from the temple hearth every hearth in the realm is lit again.
Dazh's flame burns again.

The warriors have gathered in the temple yard before the war. The priest of Tor stands at the altar with an axe in his hands and asks the old question: will the lord swear on the thunder? No flight and no surrender, until the war is won. Tor hears every oath, and Tor does not forget.
I swear it on Tor's thunder.
I will make no oath.

The war is lost, and the oath sworn on the thunder is broken. The priests of Tor will not meet your eyes, and the warriors spit when you pass. Some nights there is lightning over the steppe with no storm in it.
Tor forgives nothing.
The war is won and the oath held. The priests of Tor paint a lightning bolt on your shield in ox blood, and the warriors bang their axes on their shields when you ride by.
Tor heard the oath.

The barrow of Miska rises out of the steppe like a green wave, ringed with standing stones and old horse skulls. The Khan-Queen lies under it with her horses, her armour and, so the stories say, more gold than the Tzar's treasury. Gospodar lords come here to pray. Others come with shovels.
Pray at the Khan-Queen's tomb.
Dig for the grave goods.
At dawn the guards drag three filthy men out of a tunnel in the side of the barrow. Their sacks are full of gold rings and bronze horse harness. They beg on their knees and offer you half.
Hang them from the standing stones.
Half, you said?

The wise women have killed the old grey mare and are reading the year in her bones, as their mothers did. They throw the bones on a hide, look at them for a long time and argue in the old tongue. At last the eldest turns to you.
What do the bones say?
Throw them again. I do not like that look.

The wise women say your ancestors are hungry. They have come in the night to the grandmother's tent, wanting blood, and they will not go until they have it. A white horse would content them. A man would content them more.
Give them a white horse.
Give them a prisoner.
The dead can stay hungry.

In the dream you walk the spirit-paths across the steppe, past the tents of your ancestors, and at the end of the path a great bear is waiting. It does not attack. It looks at you, and you understand that it is asking you a question. When you wake, the priests of Ursun are already at the door.
I will follow the bear.
I keep to the ways of my mothers.

The priests of Ursun have come to court in a body, and they will not leave. [ursun_tainted.GetTitledName] has the taint of Chaos on them, they say, and it is plain for anyone to see. Kislev has fought the Wastes for a thousand years, and no Kislevite will suffer a mutant under the same roof.
Cast them out of the realm.
Throw them in the dungeon.
They are under my protection.
Ursun Wakes
The Father of Bears is awake, and Kislev is stronger for it.
The Long Sleep
The Father of Bears sleeps, the bears have turned on men, and the cults of the Dark Gods grow bold.
Cold Hearths
The flame of Dazh has gone out in the capital. Until it burns again, no hearth in the realm is truly warm.
Tor's Oath
Has sworn on the thunder: no flight and no surrender until the war is won.
Oathless
Broke an oath sworn on Tor's thunder. No warrior of Kislev forgets it.
Miska's Favour
The Khan-Queen spoke to this lord at her barrow.
Miska's Curse
Took gold from the barrow of the Khan-Queen, and the Khan-Queen remembers.
Good Omens
The horse bones promise a good year.
Ill Omens
The bones, or the ancestors, are against this lord.
Punished at Waking Day
Forgiven at Waking Day
Champion of the court
Protected from the priests
Tooth of Ursun
A tooth as long as a man's forearm, yellow and warm, taken from the Father of Bears where he lay wounded under the mountains.
Relight the Hearth
Send to the great temple in Kislev for Dazh's flame, and light the cold hearths of the realm again.
Ride to Miska's Barrow
Ride out onto the steppe to the barrow of the Khan-Queen Miska, mother of the Gospodars, and pray at her tomb.

Has not hunted a sorcerer in the last five years
Has not frozen a river in the last three years
Has not sealed a breach in the last five years
Has not trained a novice in the last five years
A novice of the Sisterhood is at the same court
The lord's men take the sorcerer and burn him.
The sorcerer escapes into the Wastes.
The sorcerer dies frozen solid, his fire still burning inside the ice.
Behind a silver mask you find a face you know from a Chekist's list, and a knife in the sleeve.
Nothing stirs all night but the music.
The novice comes down from the glacier in spring, thin and silent and stronger in the gift.
The novice comes down from the glacier with frost-blackened fingers.
The novice does not come down from the glacier.
The Hag-Mother gives you her distaff.
The Hag-Mother sends you home with more than you came with.
The hut walks away into the woods, and you are not seen again.

You stand on the ice of the Lynsk at midnight, alone, with the whole of the north in front of you. The rite of the Great Warding is older than the Sisterhood, and it asks for something that cannot be given back. You open your hands and let the cold take it: years of your life, poured into the river, into the frozen ground, into every stanitsa wall from here to the Tzar's palace.
Let the north find Kislev closed to it.

There is a sorcerer in the oblast. The cattle in three villages are dead with their eyes burned out, and the people of a fourth all dream the same dream of a burning tower. The trail runs east toward the forest.
I will hunt him myself.
Send the lord's men after him.

You find him in a village that has burned to the ground, standing in the ashes with fire running over his hands like water. He smiles when he sees you. He has always wanted to know whether ice really beats fire.
Show him.
[From.GetTitledName] has gone out onto the riverbank in the night and frozen the river from bank to bank, thick enough to carry a cannon. Your armies can cross where no bridge stands.
Across, before it thaws.

Where the daemons came through, the air is still torn. You can see it if you look sideways: a seam in the world, weeping light that is not light, with things moving behind it. The priests will not go near it. Someone has to close it.
Close it.
Leave it to the priests.

The Ice Queen's Ball is in full swing, and every face in the hall is behind a mask. The Sisterhood has always watched over the Ball, because the Ball has always drawn the crown's enemies like moths. Tonight it is your turn.
Watch the masks.
Dance. Nothing ever happens.

You take [frost_novice.GetFirstName] up onto the Frosthome glacier as the first snow falls, with a hide tent, a bag of dried fish and nothing else. For a whole winter she will live in the cold until it stops being her enemy. Many novices have made this climb. Not all of them came down.
Teach her the cold.

[frost_rival.GetTitledName] wants what is yours: the novice you found, or your seat at your lord's side, or both. She has said so in front of the court, coldly and politely, as the Sisterhood says everything. The court is waiting to see what you do.
Settle it with a duel of ice.
We are sisters. Let us be sisters.
Let her have it.

The hag [frost_hag.GetFirstName] sits by her fire with a pipe in her teeth and looks you up and down. The Sisterhood, she says, is a lot of girls playing in the snow. Her grandmother's grandmother knew magic before there was a Tzar or an Ice Palace, and she still does.
Walk away from the old woman.
Then teach me, grandmother.
Chaos is in the land. We stand together, or we fall separately.

An Ice Witch in white furs has come to your village for the girl. She has the gift, everyone knows it, and the Sisterhood will take her to Frosthome and make her one of them. The girl looks at you. So does the witch.
Go with her, child. It is a better life.
There is no girl here. Search all you like.
Take her, and take something of mine with her.

Deep in the woods, where the trees grow so close that no light reaches the snow, you find it: a hut of black logs, standing on two great scaly legs. It turns slowly to look at you. Smoke rises from the chimney. Somebody inside is singing.
Knock.
Call her by the old name.
Turn back while I still can.

The Hag-Mother is older than anything you have ever seen, and she is laughing. She sits you by her stove, feeds you soup you do not want to look at, and asks you three questions. The first is easy. The second is hard. The third, you understand, is the only one that matters.
Answer.
The Great Warding
A Grand Ice Witch has warded this land with her own life. The north finds it closed.
Toll of the Warding
Gave years of her life to the Great Warding.
Hunted a Sorcerer
Has hunted a sorcerer recently.
Froze a River
Has frozen a river recently.
Sealed a Breach
Has sealed a warp-breach recently.
Trained a Novice
Has trained a novice recently.
The Frozen River
An Ice Witch has frozen the rivers in this lord's path.
Haunted by the Breach
Looked too long into a warp-breach, and something looked back.
Old Lore
Has learned the old magic of the Ungol hags.
Pact against Chaos
An Ice Witch and a hag have sworn to stand together against the Dark Gods.
A Hidden Apprentice
Keeps a girl with the gift hidden from the Sisterhood and teaches her the old ways.
Wisdom of the Hag-Mother
Answered the Hag-Mother's questions and came home.
Warded my lands
Served me with her magic
Trained me on the glacier
Scorned me
Sworn to stand together
The Great Warding

Go to the Lynsk and pour your own life into the ice. For ten years your lord's lands in Kislev are warded against the north, and the Dark Gods lose ground. The cost is your health, for the rest of your life.
Hunt a Sorcerer
A Chaos sorcerer is hiding in the oblast. Find him, and see whether ice beats fire.
Freeze the River
Freeze the river in your lord's path so that his armies can cross where no bridge stands.
Seal the Breach
Where the daemons came through, the world is torn. Close the wound.
A Winter on the Glacier
Take a novice of your court onto the Frosthome glacier for a winter, and teach her the cold.
Seek the Hag-Mother
Go into the deep woods to find the walking hut of the Hag-Mother, the first of the hags. Some come back with gifts. Some do not come back.
Frost Maidens
Distaff of the Hag-Mother
A distaff of black wood wound with grey wool that never runs out. It is warm to the touch, even in winter.
